# What does this PR do?

Fixes two MoE bugs in the sequence-chunked MLP path (`mlp_chunks_for_training` / `mlp_chunks_for_prefill`) in `TransformerLayer._run_mlp`, which `TransformerLayer` and `HyperConnectionTransformerLayer` share:

- **EP deadlock from unequal MoE call counts.** `num_chunks` was capped at the local sequence length, and `torch.chunk` can return fewer chunks than requested (10 tokens into 8 gives 5 chunks of 2). Every MoE call runs EP all-to-alls, so a rank with a shorter local sequence (e.g. a 1-token padding micro-batch used to even out micro-batch counts across DP ranks) made fewer calls than its EP peers and the group hung. MoE layers now always make exactly `num_chunks` calls (`tensor_split`), padding a shorter sequence with masked dummy tokens whose outputs are dropped. A mask is built when the caller passed none, so the router leaves the dummies out of its aux-loss, z-loss and expert-bias counts. Dense MLPs keep the old cap.
- **Routing replay (`moe_enable_routing_replay`) with chunking.** `RouterReplay` holds one top-k tensor per micro-batch (`[s * b, topk]`), and `get_replay_topk` gathers the call's scores (`[chunk_tokens, num_experts]`) with it, so replay failed on the first chunk ("Size does not match at dimension 0"). Recompute popped one micro-batch entry per chunk, and recording kept only the last chunk's indices. The new `ChunkedRouterReplay` gives each chunk its slice of the micro-batch's indices, passed to the chunk's call as `MoELayer.forward(replay_topk_idx=...)`, and records the concatenated indices (static buffers included) after the last chunk. As an argument, the slice is also what a recompute of that call replays: with selective `"moe"` recompute, backward reruns each chunk's checkpointed MoE call on its own, not the chunk loop, in whatever order autograd picks. Full-layer recompute reruns the loop, which splits the micro-batch's `replay_backward_list` entry again.
- **Quantile balancing with a short local sequence** now raises `NotImplementedError` before any MoE call: the dummy tokens need a padding mask, which quantile balancing does not support yet (base ran this case with fewer chunks). Whether to make quantile balancing honor the mask instead is left to its maintainers.

The chunk loop moves into `TransformerLayer._run_mlp_in_chunks`; the non-chunked and recompute paths are untouched.

## Issue tracking

Linked issue: none. Found while training GLM-5.3-Flash and Qwen3.8-Flash-Next with RL (routing replay on) in SkyRL, where the same fix shipped as NovaSky-AI/SkyRL#2532.

## Code provenance

No external code. The change re-implements, for megatron-core, a fix the PR author wrote in NovaSky-AI/SkyRL#2532 (Apache-2.0).

They drive `_run_mlp_in_chunks` with a toy MoE and run on CPU: 28 pass with this change; selective `"moe"` recompute is covered with a checkpointed toy MoE, including reruns in a different order than forward. ## Strict review: MoE MLP chunking (equal EP call counts and per-chunk routing replay)

**Findings: CRITICAL 1, IMPORTANT 1, SUGGESTION 1.** Each finding is an inline comment with a failure case, a correction and acceptance checks. I read the code statically and ran no tests.

### Most impactful
1. **[CRITICAL Correctness] The routing-replay recompute fix covers only full-layer recompute** ([transformer_layer.py#L1560](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/1fdff17d5f45577c2d78de87bb077c56d607672e/megatron/core/transformer/transformer_layer.py#L1560)).
   - With selective `"moe"` recompute, each chunk's `MoELayer` checkpoint reruns the router outside `_run_mlp_in_chunks`, so `ChunkedRouterReplay` never splits the backward entry.
   - Backward then fails in `gather`. With 1-token micro-batches it can instead use the wrong routing without any error.
2. **[IMPORTANT Compatibility] Regression for quantile-balancing routers** ([transformer_layer.py#L1539](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/1fdff17d5f45577c2d78de87bb077c56d607672e/megatron/core/transformer/transformer_layer.py#L1539)).
   - When the local sequence is shorter than the chunk count, the PR now builds a padding mask that every chunk receives.
   - `TopKRouter.routing` asserts that QB gets no mask, so QB training or prefill with a short local sequence now fails, where base worked.
3. **[SUGGESTION] Shape check for replay indices** ([router_replay.py#L342](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/1fdff17d5f45577c2d78de87bb077c56d607672e/megatron/core/transformer/moe/router_replay.py#L342)).
   - The chunked path quietly cuts down replay indices that are too large; the unchunked path raises an error for them.
   - Checking the row count makes this boundary explicit.

### Checked, no issue found
- **EP call parity:** every MoE call now has at least one token, and every rank makes exactly `num_chunks` calls.
- **Capacity:** with `pad > 0` each chunk is one sequence row, so a chunk holds only real tokens or only dummy tokens. Dummy tokens cannot take capacity from real ones.
- **Split sizes:** `tensor_split` matches `chunk` whenever `num_chunks` divides `s`, so the existing `test_transformer_layer.py::test_chunked_mlp` split is unchanged.
- **Dense MLPs:** the `min(num_chunks, s)` cap is unchanged.
- **Performance:** padding uses shapes only, so it adds no host-device sync.
- **Token order:** the router flattens `[s, b]` sequence-first, which matches the slice bounds `chunk.shape[0] * batch_size`.
- **Recording:** final contents of the legacy and double-buffered static buffers match the unchunked path. The saved target is restored after the loop.
- **Imports:** `router_replay.py` imports only `torch`, so the new import in `transformer_layer.py` creates no import cycle.
- **New identifiers:** all have real uses.
- **New tests:** I traced every assertion in `test_chunked_mlp.py` against the head code and found nothing that would break them. They model full-layer recompute only, which is the gap behind finding 1.
- The two children covering routing replay and chunk padding returned results. The third child's report (tests, compatibility, style) did not reach me, so I checked those areas myself.

### Overall risk
Moderate. The EP-deadlock fix itself looks correct and well contained. Two things block approval:
- the QB regression (finding 2);
- the incomplete recompute fix for routing replay under `"moe"` recompute, which should either be completed or rejected up front with a clear error (finding 1).

**[CRITICAL Correctness]** Routing replay still breaks during selective `"moe"` recompute. Each chunk's checkpoint reruns its router outside this loop, so the backward split in `ChunkedRouterReplay` never runs.

**Why**
- MoE layers never set `recompute_mlp` ([transformer_layer.py#L581-L583](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/1fdff17d5f45577c2d78de87bb077c56d607672e/megatron/core/transformer/transformer_layer.py#L581-L583)), so they take this chunked path.
- With `recompute_granularity="selective"` and `"moe"` in `recompute_modules`, `MoELayer.forward` wraps each chunk call in `precision_aware_checkpoint` ([moe_layer.py#L275-L279](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/1fdff17d5f45577c2d78de87bb077c56d607672e/megatron/core/transformer/moe/moe_layer.py#L275-L279), [#L792-L800](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/1fdff17d5f45577c2d78de87bb077c56d607672e/megatron/core/transformer/moe/moe_layer.py#L792-L800)).
- In backward, each checkpoint calls `route()` and then the router directly. `_run_mlp_in_chunks` is not re-entered, so the split at [router_replay.py#L344-L348](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/1fdff17d5f45577c2d78de87bb077c56d607672e/megatron/core/transformer/moe/router_replay.py#L344-L348) never happens.

**Failure**
- **Trigger:** `moe_enable_routing_replay=True`, `mlp_chunks_for_training=4`, selective recompute with `"moe"`, and the documented flow: `REPLAY_FORWARD` in forward, `REPLAY_BACKWARD` during recompute ([router_replay.md#L63-L66](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/1fdff17d5f45577c2d78de87bb077c56d607672e/docs/api-guide/router_replay.md#L63-L66)).
- **Actual:**
  - Forward now passes.
  - In backward, each chunk pops the whole micro-batch entry `[s*b, topk]` ([router_replay.py#L233-L237](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/1fdff17d5f45577c2d78de87bb077c56d607672e/megatron/core/transformer/moe/router_replay.py#L233-L237)). `scores.gather` on `[chunk_tokens, E]` scores then raises `RuntimeError`.
  - If `REPLAY_FORWARD` stays on during backward, `finish()` has already restored the full target, so the same mismatch happens.
  - With 1-token micro-batches (entry size equals chunk size, the padding case this PR targets), extra chunks pop the *next* micro-batches' entries. Later recomputes are then routed wrongly with no error.
  - With `RECORD` left on during backward, recompute overwrites `recorded_topk_idx` and static-buffer rows `[:chunk_tokens]` with a single chunk's indices.
- **Expected:** each recompute routes exactly its own tokens, or the configuration is rejected up front.
- **Not a regression:** base already failed in forward. But the PR says recompute is fixed, and that holds only when the chunk loop itself reruns (full-layer recompute).

**Correction**
- **Invariant:** every router call under `REPLAY_*` receives the indices of exactly the tokens it routes, in forward and in recompute.
- A complete fix would have to bind each chunk's slice to its own checkpoint, and chunk recomputes run in reverse order. I'm not confident enough in a specific implementation to propose one.
- **Minimal safe fix:** reject the combination right after building `replay`, and narrow the `ChunkedRouterReplay` docstring ([router_replay.py#L308-L309](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/1fdff17d5f45577c2d78de87bb077c56d607672e/megatron/core/transformer/moe/router_replay.py#L308-L309)) to full-layer recompute.

# _run_mlp_in_chunks, right after `replay = ChunkedRouterReplay(...)`

    getattr(self.mlp, "moe_layer_recompute", False)
    and self.mlp.training

**Preservation**
- Full-layer recompute, which reruns this loop. The PR test `test_routing_replay_per_chunk` recompute section must still give concatenated indices `== target` and `replay_backward_list == []`.
- `"moe"` recompute without chunking: the non-chunked branch is untouched.
- No-grad replay passes (e.g. log-prob) and eval/prefill: the guard short-circuits on `is_grad_enabled()` and `training`.
- `RECORD`, no replay, and MLPs without `moe_layer_recompute` (the PR's `ToyMoE`).

**Acceptance (proposed tests, not run)**
- **Repro:** a `ToyMoE` subclass with `moe_layer_recompute = True` whose forward body runs under `torch.utils.checkpoint.checkpoint(..., use_reentrant=False)`. Use `x.requires_grad_()`, s=30, b=1, 4 chunks, `set_target_indices(target)` and `REPLAY_FORWARD`.

  - After the fix: `NotImplementedError` at forward.
- **Same setup under `torch.no_grad()`:** no error, and the indices equal `target`.
- **Regression:** all existing tests in `test_chunked_mlp.py` and `test_router_replay.py` still pass.

**[IMPORTANT Compatibility]** The mask built here for dummy tokens makes quantile-balancing (QB) MoE layers fail when the local sequence is shorter than the chunk count. This worked on base.

**Failure**
- **Trigger:** `moe_router_load_balancing_type="quantile_balancing"`, no caller `padding_mask`, and local `s < num_chunks`. Two ways to reach it:
  - `mlp_chunks_for_training=4` with hidden `[3, b, h]`;
  - `mlp_chunks_for_prefill=4` with a 3-token prefill.
- **Head:**
  1. `pad=1`.
  2. L1540-L1543 build and pad a mask, so *every* chunk, real ones included, gets a non-None `[b, 1]` mask.
  3. [`MoELayer.route`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/1fdff17d5f45577c2d78de87bb077c56d607672e/megatron/core/transformer/moe/moe_layer.py#L530-L535) forwards the mask to the router.
  4. [`TopKRouter.routing`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/1fdff17d5f45577c2d78de87bb077c56d607672e/megatron/core/transformer/moe/router.py#L1142-L1146) asserts `padding_mask is None` for QB, so the first chunk raises `AssertionError`.
- **Base** ([transformer_layer.py#L1485-L1506](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/e3f528380c197e8811fb68064d9ef3acf59fd3c6/megatron/core/transformer/transformer_layer.py#L1485-L1506)): `num_chunks=min(4, 3)` with `chunk()` and a None mask, so QB ran. With EP=1 or equal local lengths there was no deadlock.
- **Why dropping the mask for QB is not enough:** with `pad > 0` each dummy chunk is entirely dummy tokens. Unmasked, those chunks would feed into `qb_beta_accum`/`qb_beta_count` ([router.py#L508-L513](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/1fdff17d5f45577c2d78de87bb077c56d607672e/moe/router.py#L508-L513)) or the global_batch histogram (L458-L470), and routing statistics would drift with no error.

**Correction**
- **Invariant:** chunks the caller did not mask behave as on base, and dummy rows never touch routing statistics (QB beta and histogram, aux loss, z-loss, expert bias).
- **Option (a), complete fix:** make QB honor `padding_mask` by excluding masked rows from `qb_dual_update`'s quantile and from the histogram. Keep `all_gather_into_tensor`'s equal-size requirement (pass the mask through the gather, not a variable-length tensor). I haven't traced QB enough to give an exact patch.
- **Option (b), interim:** raise a clear `NotImplementedError` before any MoE call when `pad and getattr(router, "routing_type", None) == "quantile_balancing"`. The message should name `mlp_chunks_for_training`/`mlp_chunks_for_prefill` and the short local sequence. Note that (b) still disables a configuration that worked on base, so the PR description should say so.

**Preservation**
- Non-QB routers still mask dummy tokens out of aux loss, z-loss and expert bias.
- `pad == 0` is unchanged.
- MoE layers still make exactly `num_chunks` calls.
- Dense MLPs keep the `min` cap.
- A caller-supplied mask with QB still fails as on base.

**Acceptance (proposed, not run)**
- **GPU test:** QB with global_batch scope, EP=1, `mlp_chunks_for_training=4`, hidden `[3, 2, h]`, no mask, train mode.
  - Head: `AssertionError` from router.py L1143-L1145.
  - After (a): output equals the unchunked layer, and only the 6 real tokens enter `qb_histogram`.
  - After (b): `NotImplementedError` with the message above.
- **Prefill:** the same check with `mlp_chunks_for_prefill`.
- **Existing test:** `test_moe_makes_exactly_num_chunks_calls` keeps its call-count and output assertions.

**[SUGGESTION Other]** Add a shape check: the chunked path now quietly accepts replay indices with the wrong row count.

**Failure**
- **Unchunked path:** a target or recompute entry with more rows than the call's tokens raises at `scores.gather` ([L230](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/1fdff17d5f45577c2d78de87bb077c56d607672e/megatron/core/transformer/moe/router_replay.py#L230), [L237](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/1fdff17d5f45577c2d78de87bb077c56d607672e/megatron/core/transformer/moe/router_replay.py#L237)).
- **Chunked path:** each chunk takes `target[bounds[i]:bounds[i+1]]`, so the extra rows are ignored without an error.
- **Example:** under sequence parallelism, a caller that passes the full-sequence `[s*b, topk]` target instead of the rank-local `[s/tp*b, topk]` one. Every TP rank would then quietly replay the first `s/tp*b` rows.
- **Expected:** one row per real token, or a clear error.

**Correction:** check the row count on the target and on the popped recompute entry before padding. This reads only tensor metadata: no device sync, and it is safe for CUDA graphs.

# What does this PR do?

Fixes two MoE bugs in the sequence-chunked MLP path (`mlp_chunks_for_training` / `mlp_chunks_for_prefill`) in `TransformerLayer._run_mlp`, which `TransformerLayer` and `HyperConnectionTransformerLayer` share:

- **EP deadlock from unequal MoE call counts.** `num_chunks` was capped at the local sequence length, and `torch.chunk` can return fewer chunks than requested (10 tokens into 8 gives 5 chunks of 2). Every MoE call runs EP all-to-alls, so a rank with a shorter local sequence (e.g. a 1-token padding micro-batch used to even out micro-batch counts across DP ranks) made fewer calls than its EP peers and the group hung. MoE layers now always make exactly `num_chunks` calls (`tensor_split`), padding a shorter sequence with masked dummy tokens whose outputs are dropped. A mask is built when the caller passed none, so the router leaves the dummies out of its aux-loss, z-loss and expert-bias counts. Dense MLPs keep the old cap.
- **Routing replay (`moe_enable_routing_replay`) with chunking.** `RouterReplay` holds one top-k tensor per micro-batch (`[s * b, topk]`), and `get_replay_topk` gathers the call's scores (`[chunk_tokens, num_experts]`) with it, so replay failed on the first chunk ("Size does not match at dimension 0"). Recompute popped one micro-batch entry per chunk, and recording kept only the last chunk's indices. The new `ChunkedRouterReplay` gives each chunk its slice of the micro-batch's indices, passed to the chunk's call as `MoELayer.forward(replay_topk_idx=...)`, and records the concatenated indices (static buffers included) after the last chunk. As an argument, the slice is also what a recompute of that call replays: with selective `"moe"` recompute, backward reruns each chunk's checkpointed MoE call on its own, not the chunk loop, in whatever order autograd picks. Full-layer recompute reruns the loop, which splits the micro-batch's `replay_backward_list` entry again.
- **Quantile balancing with a short local sequence** now raises `NotImplementedError` before any MoE call: the dummy tokens need a padding mask, which quantile balancing does not support yet (base ran this case with fewer chunks). Whether to make quantile balancing honor the mask instead is left to its maintainers.

The chunk loop moves into `TransformerLayer._run_mlp_in_chunks`; the non-chunked and recompute paths are untouched.

Linked issue: none. Found while training GLM-5.3-Flash and Qwen3.8-Flash-Next with RL (routing replay on) in SkyRL, where the same fix shipped as NovaSky-AI/SkyRL#2532.

No external code. The change re-implements, for megatron-core, a fix the PR author wrote in NovaSky-AI/SkyRL#2532 (Apache-2.0).

+class ToyRouter(torch.nn.Module):
+    """Linear router that picks its top-k through ``RouterReplay`` like ``TopKRouter``."""
+
+    def __init__(self):
+        super().__init__()
+        self.weight = torch.nn.Linear(H, E, bias=False)
+        self.router_replay = RouterReplay()

+    def forward(self, x):
+        scores = torch.softmax(self.weight(x.reshape(-1, H)), dim=-1)
+
+        def default(scores, topk, num_groups=None, group_topk=None):
+            return torch.topk(scores, topk, dim=-1)
+
+        return self.router_replay.get_replay_topk(scores, K, None, None, default)

+class ToyMoE(torch.nn.Module):
+    """Per-token MoE stand-in: output = x * (sum of the selected experts' probs), masked to 0.
+
+    Like ``MoELayer``, it replays ``replay_topk_idx`` around its router call and, with
+    ``moe_layer_recompute``, checkpoints that call (``calls`` then also logs the recompute).
+    """
+
+    def __init__(self, moe_layer_recompute=False):
+        super().__init__()
+        self.router = ToyRouter()
+        self.moe_layer_recompute = moe_layer_recompute
+        self.calls = []
+
+    def forward(
+        self, x, padding_mask=None, packed_seq_params=None, input_ids=None, replay_topk_idx=None
+    ):
+        def custom_forward(x):
+            with RouterReplay.replay_indices_for_call(self.router.router_replay, replay_topk_idx):
+                probs, indices = self.router(x)
+            self.calls.append(
+                {
+                    "tokens": x.shape[0],
+                    "x": x.detach().clone(),
+                    "padding_mask": padding_mask,
+                    "indices": indices.clone(),
+                }
+            )
+            out = x * probs.sum(dim=-1).reshape(x.shape[0], x.shape[1], 1)
+            if padding_mask is not None:  # [b, s], True = padding
+                out = out * (~padding_mask).transpose(0, 1).unsqueeze(-1)
+            return out
+
+        if self.moe_layer_recompute and self.training:
+            out = torch.utils.checkpoint.checkpoint(custom_forward, x, use_reentrant=True)
+        else:
+            out = custom_forward(x)
+        return out, None

+    per call, and recording keeps only the last call's indices.
+

+    records the concatenated indices of all chunks once the last chunk is done.

+            pad_tokens (int): Number of dummy tokens appended after the real tokens to even out

## Strict review: MoE MLP chunking (equal EP call counts and per-chunk routing replay)

**Findings: CRITICAL 1, IMPORTANT 1, SUGGESTION 1.** Each finding is an inline comment with a failure case, a correction and acceptance checks. I read the code statically and ran no tests.

### Most impactful
1. **[CRITICAL Correctness] The routing-replay recompute fix covers only full-layer recompute** ([transformer_layer.py#L1560](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/1fdff17d5f45577c2d78de87bb077c56d607672e/megatron/core/transformer/transformer_layer.py#L1560)).
   - With selective `"moe"` recompute, each chunk's `MoELayer` checkpoint reruns the router outside `_run_mlp_in_chunks`, so `ChunkedRouterReplay` never splits the backward entry.
   - Backward then fails in `gather`. With 1-token micro-batches it can instead use the wrong routing without any error.
2. **[IMPORTANT Compatibility] Regression for quantile-balancing routers** ([transformer_layer.py#L1539](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/1fdff17d5f45577c2d78de87bb077c56d607672e/megatron/core/transformer/transformer_layer.py#L1539)).
   - When the local sequence is shorter than the chunk count, the PR now builds a padding mask that every chunk receives.
   - `TopKRouter.routing` asserts that QB gets no mask, so QB training or prefill with a short local sequence now fails, where base worked.
3. **[SUGGESTION] Shape check for replay indices** ([router_replay.py#L342](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/1fdff17d5f45577c2d78de87bb077c56d607672e/megatron/core/transformer/moe/router_replay.py#L342)).
   - The chunked path quietly cuts down replay indices that are too large; the unchunked path raises an error for them.
   - Checking the row count makes this boundary explicit.

### Checked, no issue found
- **EP call parity:** every MoE call now has at least one token, and every rank makes exactly `num_chunks` calls.
- **Capacity:** with `pad > 0` each chunk is one sequence row, so a chunk holds only real tokens or only dummy tokens. Dummy tokens cannot take capacity from real ones.
- **Split sizes:** `tensor_split` matches `chunk` whenever `num_chunks` divides `s`, so the existing `test_transformer_layer.py::test_chunked_mlp` split is unchanged.
- **Dense MLPs:** the `min(num_chunks, s)` cap is unchanged.
- **Performance:** padding uses shapes only, so it adds no host-device sync.
- **Token order:** the router flattens `[s, b]` sequence-first, which matches the slice bounds `chunk.shape[0] * batch_size`.
- **Recording:** final contents of the legacy and double-buffered static buffers match the unchunked path. The saved target is restored after the loop.
- **Imports:** `router_replay.py` imports only `torch`, so the new import in `transformer_layer.py` creates no import cycle.
- **New identifiers:** all have real uses.
- **New tests:** I traced every assertion in `test_chunked_mlp.py` against the head code and found nothing that would break them. They model full-layer recompute only, which is the gap behind finding 1.
- The two children covering routing replay and chunk padding returned results. The third child's report (tests, compatibility, style) did not reach me, so I checked those areas myself.

### Overall risk
Moderate. The EP-deadlock fix itself looks correct and well contained. Two things block approval:
- the QB regression (finding 2);
- the incomplete recompute fix for routing replay under `"moe"` recompute, which should either be completed or rejected up front with a clear error (finding 1).

**3. [SUGGESTION] Row-count check: implemented.**

- **New kwarg:** `is_moe_layer` means `isinstance(self.mlp, MoELayer)` ([transformer_layer.py#L502](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/ea8d4fbff770ed4ef1605d9d42cb5d978944f5e0/megatron/core/transformer/transformer_layer.py#L502)).
